analysis.body:
# US Grid Interconnection Queues and AI Data Center Infrastructure

Across five major US grid operators, 8,372 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million megawatts sit in interconnection queues as of mid-September 2026. ERCOT's Texas queue dominates with 438,086 MW across 1,778 requests, followed by NYISO at 319,095 MW and MISO at 299,721 MW. While these queue totals measure planned generation capacity waiting for grid connection rather than data center demand directly, storage and gas projects within these queues—totaling 328,741 MW and 184,543 MW respectively—serve as practical proxies for infrastructure following compute load, since AI facilities increasingly require both dispatchable power and battery backup to meet grid reliability rules.

Commercial-sector electricity sales across eight key states totaled 54,798 megawatt-hours in June 2026, with Texas leading at 15,754 MWh, followed by California at 10,025 MWh and Virginia at 7,771 MWh. These states correspond closely to ERCOT, CAISO, and NYISO service territories where data center clustering is densest. Prices varied sharply by region: California's commercial rate of $27.33 per MWh more than tripled Texas's $8.66, while Virginia stood at $10.99, reflecting both generation mix and transmission constraints that matter for facility siting decisions.

Solar dominates new generation requests across all queues at 277,759 MW total, but storage's 328,741 MW and gas's 184,543 MW reveal infrastructure responding to variability requirements rather than average load alone. ERCOT's gas projects (78,092 MW) and storage (159,820 MW) are substantially larger than other regions', suggesting Texas's queue reflects acute peaking and reliability pressures. Watch whether NYISO's unusually large "other" category (291,136 MW) resolves into storage or demand-response resources in coming monthly reports, as that clarification will signal whether New York's infrastructure strategy differs fundamentally from the nation's solar-plus-storage dominant pattern.
